SIL AI Engineering builds and researches AI for Bible translation: machine translation drafting, translation quality checking, speech and evaluation methods, with a focus on minority languages where the only data is often a single parallel Bible.

## How studies are published

Each study is a folder in [this site's repository](https://github.com/sillsdev/ai-research) with its write-up, a summary of the results and a `sources.yml` naming the repository and commit the results came from. The tables and charts are drawn from that summary when the site is built, so the numbers on a page are the numbers in the repository.

## What a study leaves out

Much of this research uses unpublished translation drafts and Bibles that can't be redistributed, and some translation projects work in places where naming them could put people at risk. So the studies publish aggregate results only. They don't quote draft or copyrighted text, and they refer to translation projects, teams and languages by anonymous labels unless a language is named by a public dataset.
